    "summary": "gh-1425 [GOAL] Resume loses structured-compaction folds — marathon session reopens at 143% of window make fold projection resume-equivalent and cap every detonation path",
    "description": "Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate."
  }
}

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate."

# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.

    "description": "Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate."

# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate."

    "description": "Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate."

# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.

    "description": "Closes #1425
# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

### Notes
- Healthy fold rendering is intentionally unchanged (REG-1 asserted byte-shape equality) — only unresolvable folds change behavior, and only by becoming visible notes instead of silent half-applies.
- The resume note is one user-role message; it adds no hidden context and keeps the `window − reserve` invariant via the existing pre-flight gate."

# gh-1425 — Resume loses structured-compaction folds (marathon session)

### Root Cause
Resuming a marathon session did not reproduce the live fold projection — three legs:
- `WindowedSessionStorage.growOlderUntil` stopped the resume boundary walk when the branch *contained* the newest classic compaction record, but the kept region starts at `firstKeptEntryId` — a walk block-bottom landing inside the kept span silently dropped the whole kept region (residency skew), so folds half-applied over a different record population.
- `renderStructuredMessages` applied every fold record as-is, with no resolution check: a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (an older writer stored the ids under keys this build does not read — empty id shape) still rendered its checkpoint text as a valid summary over nothing.
- Resume boot never capped an over-window session (the meter sat at 143% and waited); and the degraded local-trim valve kept `keepRecentTokens` *transcript* tokens while the trigger measures *request* tokens (incl. system-prompt/tool overhead), so a degraded boot landed back over the trigger and re-fired compaction on turn 1.

### Fix
- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`: `growOlderUntil` now keeps paging until the classic boundary's `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) — the resumed replay sees the full kept path.
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/projection.dart`: all-or-note fold resolution — a fold the replaying binary cannot resolve (empty id shape: an older writer's keys this build does not read) is dropped WHOLE, never applied, and a visible resume note names it (seq + kind). Off-path references (off-branch checkpoint coverage, below-window ranges) are not skew and render exactly as before (REG-1).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` + `session_commands.dart`: resume boot cap — `_loadSession` runs one gated forced compaction pass at idle boot (also on mid-REPL session switches) so the meter renders the post-cap number before the first user message.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: `_localTrimFallback` clamps its kept budget to `min(keepRecentTokens, trigger − overhead)` so a degraded (summarizer-down) boot stays under the compaction trigger and the session remains usable without a working summarizer.

### Test Coverage
- `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — boundary walk keeps paging until `firstKeptEntryId` is resident (RED before fix).
- `test/compaction/structured_resume_equivalence_test.dart` — live-vs-resume projection byte-shape equality over a marathon fixture with a forked branch and folded checkpoints; AC2 tests: empty-shape hidden range and checkpoint dropped whole with a note, off-path refs apply unchanged with no note.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — AC3: cap pass runs before any user input and the next request fits the window; AC5: dead summarizer degrades to the visible `[context trimmed]` note, boot survives, turn 1 answers without re-firing compaction.
- Full suite: `dart test test/compaction test/agent test/cli` green (see notes on the earlier native abort).

# Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —

# Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then

# gh-1300 AC6: the shard duration-budget gate's own red exits are
      # fixture-self-tested (breach fails + files the body; fit passes;
      # warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
      # ratchet cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes

1. `resolveStructuredFolds` — `seqs` parameter unused. Confirm: the body never references `seqs`. Yes — looking at the function, `seqs` is not used. Dead parameter. SUGGESTION.

2. `renderStructuredMessages`: `droppedById` — variable naming fine. Note: if a dropped fold record appears TWICE in path (same id twice — impossible). OK.

3. Consider: dropped fold CHECKPOINT that is also referenced as `cover` by... a dropped checkpoint never enters `covered`, so records it covered render normally. Good (all-or-note).

4. What about `_hiddenToolCallIds` — for a dropped checkpoint's covered records: they render normally, so their tool calls are on the wire. But what about records that were hidden by a HEALTHY hidden_range AND covered by a DROPPED checkpoint? state.hiddenRecordIds still contains them (healthy range applied) → they render as markers. Consistent.

5. Subtle: a dropped checkpoint cc2 covers [a, b]; a LATER healthy checkpoint cc4's coversRecordIds includes cc2 itself (flattenedRecordIds...). In `buildStructuredViewState` and `resolveStructuredFolds`, `covered[cc2] = cc4` — cc2 dropped note still renders because the renderer checks `droppedById` BEFORE `_projectRecord` (which would have suppressed it as covered). Good ordering: the note renders even if a later checkpoint covers the dropped one. OK.

6. Now the note message: `UserMessage.text(...)` with `timestamp: record.timestamp`. Two consecutive dropped folds → two notes. Fine.

7. The note text: "structured fold #${seq ?? '?'}" — seq is the JSONL line number in the FULL file. In a windowed resume, `RecordSeqIndex` is built over `getEntries()` (all resident entries? or whole file?). In `_projectMessages`: `final entries = await getEntries(); final seqs = RecordSeqIndex(entries);` — for windowed storage, `getEntries()` returns resident records only (the window). Hmm — then seqOf(record.id) for records outside the window returns null. The note uses `seq ?? '?'` — handles null. Fine. But wait — this is pre-existing behavior for markers too (hiddenMarker uses `seqs.seqOf(record.id) ?? 0`). OK.

8. REG-1: healthy-fold rendering unchanged — `resolveStructuredFolds` vs `buildStructuredViewState`: for a healthy checkpoint, both add `covered[firstRecordId]` and `covered[lastRecordId]` even when '' — identical. 9. `DroppedFold`/`ResolvedFolds`/`resolveStructuredFolds` — public in lib/src, not exported in barrel? Let me check the barrel for projection.dart exports.

10. The windowed storage fix `_keptPathResident`: verified consistent with `_applyCompactionTransform` (last CompactionRecord in root-first order).

Edge: MULTIPLE compaction records — `_keptPathResident` checks only the NEWEST one. The older compaction records' kept regions: the classic transform only uses the newest compaction record, so consistency holds.

Edge: `firstKeptEntryId` references a record that exists but is on ANOTHER branch: walk pages to file top (bounded by maxPages=512 doubling blocks — could read a huge file; but the CLI passes tokenBudget so the budget stop applies... wait, no! Look at the loop order:

```dart
if (branch.any(found) && _keptPathResident(branch)) return true;
if (tokenBudget != null) { if (estimate >= budget) { trim; return true; }
if (!_hasOlder) return true;
```

If found matched (a compaction record IS on the branch) but kept path is not resident, and branch tokens < budget → keeps paging. Eventually either budget trips (trim+stop) or file top. So bounded by budget. Good — CLI always passes a budget. The doc comment says "the [tokenBudget] stop is unaffected". Consistent with the new test.

BUT: the budget stop only fires if `estimateProjectedBranchTokens(branch) >= tokenBudget`. Consider a session with a compaction record whose firstKeptEntryId is on a side branch, and a small file: pages to file top, returns true — fine.

Consider a HUGE marathon (470MB, mostly ledger payloads pricing zero): budget never trips because ledger payloads count zero → walk pages the ENTIRE file (10s+ / 470MB) — the exact cost gh-968's budget was meant to bound. Previously the found-stop fired at the boundary record. Now, for a file where firstKeptEntryId is NOT reachable (corrupt or cross-branch id), the walk regresses to full-file paging. How likely is an unreachable firstKeptEntryId? The id is written by this same binary pointing at a record on the same branch. Cross-branch: compaction record is on the active branch; firstKeptEntryId points to ancestor — always on the branch by construction. Corrupt file (truncated parentId chain): possible. The walk still terminates (file top). Acceptable risk; the resume still works (renders fold-consistent tail... well, actually renders everything). Not a blocker; worth a note? It's defensive enough — the doubling walk was already designed to page everything for no-match sessions ("A session without a match pages everything — the whole chain is then resident and the walk reports true"). So the regression is only for match-but-unreachable-kept-start files, which are pathological. OK.

The AC5 path prints `[context trimmed]` via hooks. But an unexpected throw (e.g., a bug in the structured engine) prints NOTHING to the user — the meter stays over 100% silently (the exact symptom gh-1425 complains about). The diagnostic log goes to the shared log file. Hmm — "the meter was honest, but nothing ever capped" — after a failed cap, the meter will again show >100% and nothing tells the user why the boot didn't cap. A dim note (`io.writeln(_style.dim(...))`) would match the repo's "never silent" pattern (e.g. over-window relief logs, `[context trimmed]` note). I'd flag this as IMPORTANT — a failed boot cap is invisible to the user; the whole PR is about making over-window states visible. Let me check …

blocks.text:
# Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

      # gh-1199 AC6/E3: the flake quarantine list itself must stay
      # honest — every entry documented (issue, since, >=2 proving runs)
      # and pointing at an existing integration-tagged file.
      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)
        run: python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check

      # gh-1296 NG1/AC2: every lockfile in the repo is committed and
      # enforced — ONE inventory list (scripts/check_lockfiles.sh) fails the
      # PR when a listed lockfile is missing, untracked, or gitignored, and
      # the guard's own red exits are fixture-self-tested so the check
      # cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Lockfile inventory gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh inventory

      - name: Lockfile gate self-test (gh-1296 AC2)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles_selftest.sh
{"command":"sed -n '360,430p' .github/workflows/ci.yml"}

# gh-1300 AC6: the shard duration-budget gate's own red exits are
      # fixture-self-tested (breach fails + files the body; fit passes;
      # warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
      # ratchet cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes

blocks.text:
# Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

      # gh-1199 AC6/E3: the flake quarantine list itself must stay
      # honest — every entry documented (issue, since, >=2 proving runs)
      # and pointing at an existing integration-tagged file.
      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)
        run: python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check

      # gh-1296 NG1/AC2: every lockfile in the repo is committed and
      # enforced — ONE inventory list (scripts/check_lockfiles.sh) fails the
      # PR when a listed lockfile is missing, untracked, or gitignored, and
      # the guard's own red exits are fixture-self-tested so the check
      # cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Lockfile inventory gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh inventory

      - name: Lockfile gate self-test (gh-1296 AC2)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles_selftest.sh
{"command":"sed -n '360,430p' .github/workflows/ci.yml"}

# gh-1300 AC6: the shard duration-budget gate's own red exits are
      # fixture-self-tested (breach fails + files the body; fit passes;
      # warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
      # ratchet cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.

Consider a HUGE marathon (470MB, mostly ledger payloads pricing zero): budget never trips because ledger payloads count zero → walk pages the ENTIRE file (10s+ / 470MB) — the exact cost gh-968's budget was meant to bound. Previously the found-stop fired at the boundary record. Now, for a file where firstKeptEntryId is NOT reachable (corrupt or cross-branch id), the walk regresses to full-file paging. How likely is an unreachable firstKeptEntryId? The id is written by this same binary pointing at a record on the same branch.       # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"

# Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  C4D_VER=$(dart pub global list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="crap4dart"{print $2}')
  case "$C4D_VER" in
    # gh-1106: floor 0.11.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml duplication block
    # uses 0.11.0-only keys (ignore_locals/ignorable); the strict config
    # parser throws ConfigException on unknown keys, so older pins fail
    # rather than silently run without Type-2 detection.
    0.1[1-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*|[1-9].*)
      echo "🧪 crap4dart gates (staged core files)..."
      # gh-1106: --baseline — the Type-2 duplication gate ships with a

The pre-commit hook AUTO-FORMATS staged files (self-healing). So commits made by an agent without the hook installed (or with --no-verify, or via the factory which may not run hooks) can land unformatted. CI's static stage runs `dart analyze` but NOT `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`. So unformatted files will NOT redden CI.

So the unformatted files are not a CI gate break — they're a style inconsistency with the repo's format policy (the pre-commit self-heals; these commits evidently bypassed it — the "WIP auto-save" commits). 5 of 8 files are not format-clean. Since the repo convention is format-clean Dart (the hook auto-formats), this is a legitimate finding: IMPORTANT (the repo's established pattern; the hook would have fixed it — the author's commits bypassed the hook). # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"

          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical

#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
